73ccb11a4e: Using the MDA framework, the systems are split into mechanics, dynamics and aesthetics, and every conclusion is written as a chain: which rule → what players do because of it → what they feel. Yiren Zhi Xia, from the same studio group, serves as the A/B comparison. Based on the live version of October 2026 and a V12 account.

7f0a002e69: Naruto Mobile makes ninjas its single core product and sells them to skill-focused and progression-focused players at the same time through two opposite PvP rule sets: the Arena normalizes stats, while Ranked Points matches settle by power rating.
9ffb8d7b9c: 3 currency tiers, 8 recruit entry points, 7 progression systems; the Arena normalizes power, Ranked Points matches settle by power
aeb48bdfd8: Premium Recruit gives S-rank shards at 11.5%, with one guaranteed per ten-pull; every V12 perk is about extra attempts
8cc825856f: Arena players spend in bursts around new ninjas, power players spend daily on stamina; level caps gate time, attempt caps gate output, and money can only loosen the attempt caps
b528901c70: Raid levels 110–160 in 5 tiers; the magic-resist threshold for Secret Realm accessories rises about 10% per tier
418f6b44b6: The Arena offers challenge and expression, the power line offers achievement and collection; the same release of a strong ninja moves whales and free players in opposite emotional directions
dee8bca14e: A strong paid ninja swept the Arena at launch and was later nerfed
1ffa954fb5: Both games come from Tencent's Magic Cube studio group and are anime-IP fighting games, but their monetization goes in opposite directions.
f35f4ff844: What is soldOwnership and quantityNaruto sells ninjas, scrolls, summons and power; Yiren Zhi Xia publicly states that characters are free through log-in rewards and quests, and monetizes mainly through skins.
a441994222: How fairness worksPartly shielded / fully shieldedNaruto shields stats in some modes and uses ban slots to make a deep ninja roster valuable again; Yiren Zhi Xia shields level and gear across all of PvP.
88fc58139f: RisksOpposite directionsNaruto risks power creep and an ever-deeper power line; Yiren Zhi Xia risks a low ceiling on cosmetic spending, and breaking its fairness promise once progression enters PvP.
b111016eaa: MethodOne chain per conclusionTo keep MDA from turning into labeling, every conclusion runs from rule to player behavior to emotion, backed by in-game screenshots as evidence.
ebafcbbb0a: Each ninja serves both progression lines, so one release sells to two kinds of players, giving revenue both peaks and a stable base.
f952461217: Anti-frustration rules sit in the low and middle ranks: no points lost on a defeat at low rank, and a rank floor in the middle.
8c77cfc738: Level gates advance only with time and money can only add attempts, which keeps the rate of content consumption under control.
31c9e3650a: Free players can never get coupon-channel ninjas, and have no chance to practice against them while they are strong.
50f4a382a6: Premium Recruit only discloses the guaranteed S-rank shard per ten-pull, not how many pulls it takes to max an S-rank ninja.
d5a0686d56: The power line already has 7 progression systems, so the catch-up cost for returning and new players rises every year.
7e7015f0ce: Show pity progress for Premium Recruit, consistent with the luck meter already used in Wish Treasure.
de21954521: Four weeks after a paid ninja launches, add it to a “free this week” Arena rotation that grants play access only.
636acfefdc: Borrow Yiren Zhi Xia's separate PvE and PvP skill kits, so a new ninja's Arena strength and Ranked Points strength can be tuned independently.

ad331deb3b: Battlegrounds has no card collection: 8 players share one minion pool, and the result depends almost entirely on in-match resource decisions. This teardown looks only at a single match: how Gold comes in and is spent, how the minion pool limits choice, and how the gap between strong and weak boards opens up and is then reined in. Based on Season 14, October 2026.
463808d376: Copies of a Tier 6 minion7scarcity set by copy count
4bb80568f2: Gold cap10+1 per turn, capped on turn 8
d2d665aace: The core tension: 8 players with identical income share one minion pool, yet every match has to play out differently. The gap between strong and weak has to open up, but not decide the match too early.
88b5e77f83: Finding 1Income and prices are fixed; differences come only from spendingGold rises by 1 per turn to a cap of 10 on turn 8, and every minion costs 3. Each turn comes down to levelling the Tavern or buying power, with health as the stake.
d5d6fc976e: Finding 2Scarcity comes from copy counts, not odds tablesA Tier 6 card has only 7 copies in the whole lobby, and one triple takes 43% of them. The shared pool also creates a mind game around contested tribes and reading opponents.
3599b5900c: Finding 3Snowballing comes from the board, and it has brakesThere is no interest or win-streak bonus, and there are damage caps, copy limits and Discovers only one tier up; hero strength is balanced by converting armor into health.
3bba18de54: Finding 4Add one seasonal mechanic, remove oneEach season's new mechanic is an extra choice outside the shop. The underlying economy stays fixed, and only one or two extra systems are live at a time.
666f63853f: Payment only buys choice. The season pass widens the starting hero pick from 2 to 4, plus cosmetics. It sells no in-match stats, but the number of hero options still affects ranked play.
962b137d11: The experience centers on challenge and exploration, serving mainly achievers and explorers. Since only the top 4 gain rating, 5th place hurts the most and makes players most eager to queue again. Social play is this mode's weak spot.
8c04dffce2: Compared with Naruto Mobile: Naruto's progression accumulates over months and years, and payment can buy progress directly; Battlegrounds compresses progression into a single match and payment barely touches in-match stats, so the system design lives in the economy curve, the scarcity of shared resources and the pace at which strong and weak boards diverge.
